An honest comparison

When a private car makes sense in Madinah

Madinah has public buses, regular taxis and a railway to Makkah. A private transfer earns its place in these situations:

  • Hotel-to-hotel with luggage

    One vehicle from door to nearest permitted drop-off, with no station or bus change.

  • Families and elderly passengers

    Fewer transfers, space to board slowly, and a car that waits while you visit a site.

  • Several Ziyarat stops

    One booking for Quba, Qiblatayn, Uhud and back, instead of re-hailing at each site.

  • Late or early flights

    Pickup is worked back from your flight at any hour, and your flight is tracked.

  • Travelling on from Madinah

    Makkah, Jeddah, AlUla or Riyadh in the same vehicle, with stops on request.

  • Groups that stay together

    One fare for the whole car, or a van or coaster for larger parties.

Private car, train or bus between Madinah and Makkah?

All three work. They suit different travellers — here is the trade-off.

Qualitative comparison of a private car, the Haramain train and an intercity bus between Madinah and Makkah
  Private car Haramain trainIntercity bus
Door to doorCar:Yes — hotel to hotel or airport to hotelTrain:Station to station; onward transport needed at each endBus:Station to station; onward transport needed at each end
LuggageCar:All bags in one vehicle, loaded by the driverTrain:Carried through the stationsBus:Carried to and from the bus station
Family or groupCar:One fare for the whole carTrain:A ticket per personBus:A ticket per person
TimetableCar:You choose the departure, 24/7Train:Fixed departuresBus:Fixed departures
Stops on the wayCar:Prayer, meal or luggage stops on requestTrain:NoneBus:Set stops only

The Haramain high-speed railway runs between Madinah and Makkah and is often a good choice for a solo traveller on a fixed schedule. Check current timetables and fares with the operator — we do not publish train times because they change. Choose a private car when you travel as a family or group, carry luggage or need stops that a timetable does not give you.

Hotels near Masjid an-Nabawi

Transfers to and from the Central Area (Markaziyah)

The Central Area is the district around Al-Masjid an-Nabawi where most pilgrim hotels stand. Vehicle access there is restricted, so the driver uses the nearest permitted drop-off point to your hotel.

What to expect at a hotel near the mosque

  • Give us the exact hotel name — it decides which permitted drop-off point the driver uses.
  • Prayer times and Fridays can slow or restrict the roads around the mosque; the pickup time allows for it.
  • Porters or a short walk may be needed from the drop-off point, so tell us about heavy bags or mobility needs.
  • From MED the Central Area is about 20 km (~25 min); the Markaziyah airport route page covers hotel-level detail.
MED to Markaziyah hotels Hotel transfer service

Hotel to hotel or hotel to station

Any Madinah hotel works — send the name and the leg you need (airport, station, another hotel or a city). We do not claim any hotel partnership; the driver meets you at your confirmed hotel.

Plan your timing

What changes journey times in Madinah

Drive times shift with the season, the hour and prayer times. These are the things that move them.

01

Around Masjid an-Nabawi

Vehicle access in the Central Area (Markaziyah) next to Al-Masjid an-Nabawi is restricted and busy around prayer times. Your driver uses the nearest permitted drop-off point to your hotel and tells you where to meet on the way back.

02

Fridays and peak prayers

Roads around the mosque are slowest around Friday prayers and the main congregational prayers. Allow extra time for a flight or an intercity departure that day.

03

Umrah peaks and Ramadan

Hotel-area traffic and the roads to Makkah are heavier in Ramadan and peak Umrah weeks. Book vans and SUVs early and leave more margin for airport departures.

04

Night and early-morning arrivals

Many international flights land at night or before dawn. Transfers run 24/7 — pre-book so the car is waiting rather than searched for after a long flight.

05

Luggage and gifts

Umrah and Ziyarat travellers often carry more than planned, including dates and gifts on the way home. Tell us the number of large cases so the vehicle is sized to match.

06

Summer heat

In the hottest months plan outdoor Ziyarat stops for early morning or after sunset, with the car close by between stops.

First time in Madinah?

Terms you will see, in plain English

How do I get from Madinah Airport to my hotel?

The simplest way is a pre-booked private car from MED to your hotel — about 20 km and ~25 min, with your luggage in the same vehicle. We track your flight, so a delay moves the pickup.

What is the Central Area (Markaziyah)?

It is the district around Al-Masjid an-Nabawi where most pilgrim hotels stand. Vehicle access there is restricted, so drivers use the nearest permitted drop-off point to your hotel.

What is Ziyarat?

Ziyarat means visiting historic and religious sites. In Madinah that usually means Quba Mosque, Masjid al-Qiblatayn, the Seven Mosques area and Mount Uhud. We provide the car; we do not provide a guide.

What is a Miqat?

A Miqat is the boundary where people travelling for Umrah or Hajj enter the state of ihram. For travellers leaving Madinah it is Dhul Hulayfah (Abyar Ali). What you should do there is a religious question for a qualified scholar; we only handle the transport.

Can the car wait while we visit a site?

Yes. On a Ziyarat or private-driver booking the car waits at each stop, so you do not search for a ride afterwards. Tell us the stops and who is travelling when you book.

How do I pay?

Cash to the driver or bank transfer. An electronic receipt is available on request.

FAQ

Madinah transfer questions, answered

Short answers to what travellers ask before booking.

Ask on WhatsApp

How do I book a private transfer in Madinah?

Send your pickup, drop-off, date, passengers and luggage by the form or on WhatsApp. We reply with the vehicle and one fixed fare before anything is booked — no meter and no surge. Cancellation is free up to 24 hours before pickup.

How far is Madinah Airport (MED) from central Madinah?

Prince Mohammad bin Abdulaziz International Airport (MED) is about 20 km from the Central Area, ~25 min on a clear road. Traffic near Masjid an-Nabawi at prayer times can add to that. We track your flight and the first 15–30 minutes of waiting is free.

Can the driver take me to the door of my hotel near Masjid an-Nabawi?

The driver takes you as close as vehicles are permitted. Access around Al-Masjid an-Nabawi is restricted and varies with prayer times, so the driver uses the nearest permitted drop-off point to your hotel and tells you where to meet for the return.

Do you offer Madinah Ziyarat by car?

Yes. A private car takes you between the sites you choose — such as Quba Mosque, Masjid al-Qiblatayn, the Seven Mosques area and Mount Uhud — and waits at each stop. We provide transport only, not a guide or religious guidance.

Can I book a private driver in Madinah for several hours?

Yes. Book a car and driver for a block of hours or a full day; the car waits between stops. Send your date, start time and hours needed and we confirm the fare before booking. A single transfer is simpler when you only have one or two stops.

Can you take me from Madinah to Makkah?

Yes. Madinah to Makkah is about 430 km and ~4 hr of driving, hotel to hotel, with prayer and rest stops on request. The return trip can be booked at the same time, and Makkah to Madinah runs the other way.

Can I stop at Dhul Hulayfah (Abyar Ali) on the way to Makkah?

Ask for a stop at Dhul Hulayfah when you book a Madinah to Makkah transfer and we confirm it as part of the quote. Whether to enter ihram there is a personal religious matter we cannot advise on — please ask a qualified scholar.

Can you take me from Madinah to Jeddah Airport?

Yes. Madinah to King Abdulaziz International Airport (JED) is about 410 km, ~3 hr 50 min. We work the pickup back from your flight time. The reverse, Jeddah Airport to Madinah, is also available and we track your flight.

Can you take me from Madinah to AlUla?

Yes. Madinah to AlUla is about 330 km, roughly ~3 hr by road. A private car goes door to door to your AlUla hotel or the airport, and AlUla to Madinah is booked the same way.

Can families travel with luggage?

Yes. A sedan fits one to three people with normal luggage. A GMC or full-size SUV, or a Hyundai Staria, suits families with more luggage. A Hiace van or coaster suits larger groups. Tell us passengers and large bags and we confirm the vehicle when we quote.

How much is a private transfer in Madinah?

It depends on the route, the vehicle and the time. We do not publish fixed price lists because they would not be accurate: you send the trip and we confirm one fixed fare on WhatsApp before booking. There is no meter and no surge pricing.

Do the drivers speak English?

Yes. Drivers in our partner network speak English and Arabic, and trips run 24 hours a day.
